Rule 90 was the earlier reading here and does not reach this configuration, saying in terms that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed. That the name is anarthrous does not make the article substantival: rule 31's anarthrous-head clause (καρπὸν δικαιοσύνης τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ) is scoped to a following prepositional phrase, which has no verb to carry a relativizer, whereas a participle does. Reading τοῦ ἀπολομένου as a substantival apposition — *Zachariah, the one who perished* — and giving the article the *who* under rule 90 remains defensible, and is what the verse pass took.
